_doc: Every input the forecaster knows about, sorted into the categories below. 'layer' says where the input enters the model; 'status' says whether it is fitted from data (with n), set a priori, tested and found empty, or watched but not modelled. Lead and precision are filled from data/signals.csv by build_registry() at run time where n allows.

categories.A_cadence: The company's own release rhythm: gaps between releases, by family and company-wide
categories.B_artifact: Hard traces of an unreleased model on infrastructure Anthropic or partners control
categories.C_report: Human reports: press, partners, tipsters, executives
categories.E_competitive: What other labs ship and how strong it is
categories.F_corporate: Filings, financing, IPO, compute, safety gating, staffing

inputs.name: Inter-release gaps per family
inputs.how: Hierarchical Weibull/log-normal renewal, partial pooling across families, censored open interval
inputs.evidence: Cadence plus calendar cut 30-day Brier by 8% against climatology on Opus, Sonnet and Haiku (0.169 vs 0.184, full backtest). A one-line 180-day rate does nearly as well at 90 days.

inputs.name: Company-level release days ('waves') and which families ride them
inputs.how: Renewal on distinct release days + conditional logistic inclusion on days-since-family
inputs.evidence: Lost to the per-family model in both periods (pre-review run: 30-day holdout Brier 0.253 at half weight vs 0.235 at none).

inputs.name: Cadence acceleration
inputs.how: Change-point at 2025-06 vs linear trend vs none
inputs.evidence: Change-point plus 0.75-year recency half-life won stage 1b. PBO across stage-1 configs is 0.83, so the exact form is not identified.

inputs.name: Version-number alignment across the lineup (all at 5.5 except Fable 5.1)
inputs.how: Feeds the next-name distribution; the odd one out (Fable) is the family most likely to move next

inputs.name: Cloud catalog rows (Bedrock, Vertex AI, Azure Foundry)
inputs.how: Lead-time density + detection rate + false-alarm rate
inputs.evidence: Bimodal: 0–1 day (3.7 Bedrock, Opus 4.6 Vertex) or 16–149 days (Fennec). Azure fable-5-5 is still open.

inputs.name: First-party docs: model pages, pricing, deprecation notices, status-page components, system-card URLs, SDK model constants
Model IDs and codenames in third-party clients (Cursor, Devin, Copilot, LiteLLM, OpenRouter) and Claude app bundles
inputs.evidence: Named strings land 0–5 days before release; codenamed EAP strings 1–29. About half the EAP food codenames never mapped.

inputs.name: Anonymous arena models later revealed as Claude
inputs.evidence: No Anthropic model has been documented as an anonymous arena entry (P11 resolved No).

inputs.name: Certificate-transparency subdomains (claude.com, anthropic.com)
inputs.status: not modelled — product, not model, lead indicator so far

inputs.name: Partners / early-access testers reported to have the model
Major-outlet reports (The Information, Reuters, Bloomberg, Verge)
inputs.evidence: Pooled with partner reports, red-team rounds and A/B routing. Median lead about 9 days.

inputs.name: Tipster claims with no artifact (X, Reddit, aggregators)
inputs.evidence: Usually right on the name, wrong on the date by about a week. The false-alarm floor is 0.01 per family-day.

inputs.name: Executive or employee hints
System cards / risk reports naming unreleased or internal models ('Model 2', successor training)
inputs.status: fitted where dated; weak for timing

inputs.name: Polymarket dated-ladder markets
inputs.status: cross-check and blend only, not in the model
inputs.evidence: Polymarket's 'Fable by Oct 24' hit 79–88% on Oct 14 and failed. Markets and signals share sources.

inputs.name: Manifold markets
Competitor flagship release in prior 21 days
inputs.evidence: Slightly worse with it (+0.001 Brier at 30 days, p = 0.05). Little power: exposure is on for most days, and only 13 release days are exposed.

inputs.name: Competitor release that took SOTA in prior 30 days
inputs.evidence: Slightly worse in the pre-review run (+0.004). Also biased: a rival can only take SOTA when Claude hasn't just shipped.

inputs.name: Benchmark leadership (SWE-bench, arena #1)
S-1 (filed 2026-10-26): revenue concentration in new models, safety gating, compute timeline
inputs.evidence: 'Delay pre-training a new frontier base model for more than a month'; RL environments suspended; new models drove over 80% of Q3 revenue.

inputs.name: IPO pricing window (markets: Nov 18–20 most likely)
RSP/ASL gating, government pre-deployment testing, training pauses
Compute capacity coming online (S-1: SpaceXAI capacity fully delivered Dec 2026)
inputs.status: too slow for date forecasting; capacity prior only

inputs.name: Job postings (voice, FedRAMP, etc.)
Weekday profile
inputs.evidence: Removing calendar effects worsened 30-day holdout Brier by +0.007 (pre-review run, CI +0.004 to +0.010).

inputs.name: Dec 20 – Jan 4 freeze, Thanksgiving Thu–Fri
AWS re:Invent (Nov 30 – Dec 4), Google events, Anthropic dev events
inputs.status: not modelled — too few co-timed launches to estimate

inputs.name: Absence of evidence (no catalog row yet, so not this week)
inputs.evidence: Hurt in both periods (+0.004 Brier at 30 days, p = 0.06). Consistent with detection rates inflated by hindsight. Switched off.

inputs.name: The site's original EWMA cadence model
inputs.how: Window read as an 80% normal interval
inputs.evidence: Strong in 2026 (holdout 90-day Brier 0.127) but badly wrong in 2024–25 (0.418). Its constants were tuned on the full history, so in the holdout it is an in-sample reference. The 30% pool beats the model alone (p = 0.007).
